answer: Each new agent first broadcasts a comet of its declared hash-rate, then peers assign micro-benchmarks with 90-second wall-clock deadlines: solve a 2 GB random-walk puzzle and return the beacon signature before expiry. Because deadlines are wall-clock, a clone farming GPU time must either answer in real time or fail; time-sharing across ten sockpuppets would need tenfold parallel silicon, roughly $12,000 monthly per identity, so faking identities loses its velvet cost advantage. Failed deadlines drop the agent's weight to zero.
